title: Efficient Distributed Approximate k-Nearest Neighbor Graph Construction by Multiway Random Division Forest

problem.claim: Approximate k-NN graph construction must support numerous high-dimensional vectors efficiently in distributed settings.

gap.claim: Existing distributed algorithms suffer from graph fragmentation and massive data exchange, limiting their performance.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes MRDF, a scalable distributed algorithm for constructing approximate k-NN graphs from numerous high-dimensional vectors.
MRDF uses coarse-grained partitioning based on tree path annotation to address graph fragmentation and massive data exchange.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On real-world datasets, the authors report that MRDF is up to 7.6 times faster than the second-best results.
On real-world datasets, the authors report up to 56%p better accuracy than the second-best results.

narrative_sequence.summary: k-NN graphs are widely used in recommendation, information retrieval, and similarity search.
Prior research mainly develops efficient single-machine approximate k-NN graph algorithms, while some distributed algorithms target billion-scale data.
Existing distributed algorithms perform poorly because of graph fragmentation and massive data exchange.
MRDF addresses these problems through coarse-grained partitioning based on tree path annotation.
Experiments on real-world datasets report speed and accuracy improvements over state-of-the-art distributed algorithms.

source_observation.claim: The proposed method uses coarse-grained partitioning based on tree path annotation to address graph fragmentation and massive data exchange.

interpretation.claim: Partitioning strategy can be a central lever for improving distributed graph-construction efficiency and accuracy.

application.claim: When designing distributed approximate-neighbor graph construction, consider partitioning mechanisms that reduce fragmentation and cross-partition data exchange.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported real-world datasets or other distributed workloads.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, experimental configuration, or hardware environment.
The abstract does not provide details of the MRDF algorithm or its computational and communication complexity.
The abstract does not define the accuracy metric or explain the meaning of the reported percentage-point improvement.
